jaspreet: quick follow-up on continuous-batcher rehydration behavior. we keep seeing a short enqueue-to-serve tail for tenants that were evicted ~1-2s before a burst. sketching fixes here. link: https://rfc.internal/continuous-batcher#rehydration

lena: can you paste a tiny repro or a trace snippet?

jaspreet: repro: low-rate tenant (1 req/min) loses soft-lease after 60s. when it bursts, allocate latency adds ~150-300ms to the tail. trace:
```
trace=tx-7c3a
0ms enqueue
60005ms lease_expire
60120ms burst_enqueue
60285ms allocate_done
60310ms serve_start
```

diego: two approaches discussed earlier: transient loan pool vs extended grace-state on lease expiry. transient pool = allocator-level loan of short-lived tokens; grace-state = small retained credit in lease manager for G ms.

sarah: transient loans are easier to ship as a probe. we should limit global % and per-tenant caps to avoid cost regressions.

lena: what safety knobs?

diego: proposal: global transient cap = 5% of pool, per-tenant max = 40 tokens, loan ttl = 200ms, cooldown per-tenant = 500ms exponential backoff. include metrics: transient_loans_total, transient_loan_reclaims, rehydrate_latency_ms, lease_eviction_count.

jaspreet: experiment: enable transient loans for a small internal cohort for 24h. success if 95p enqueue_to_serve reduces by >20% and token-cost delta <1.5%.

sarah: implementation note: allocator API currently allocate_for_tenant(tenant, tokens, mode). add mode=transient -> borrow_transient under the hood. keep visible in short-term telemetry, exclude from autoscaler triggers.

lena: will own metrics PR and dashboard. jaspreet: can you open the allocator PR and experiment infra? diego: you'll draft the runbook changes (alarms: transient_usage_growth >10%/hr).

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: batcher/transient-loans -> canary-2 at 2024-05-04T08:30:00Z :rocket:

jaspreet: thanks. I'll post A/B results once the dashboard is live. objections? :eyes:
